skill.displayName: Pet Picky Eater Detection | 宠物选择性拒食识别

llm.summary: The skill’s pet-video analysis function is mostly coherent, but it automatically creates/uses backend identities and stores authentication tokens without clear user control.

dimensions.detail: Cloud video analysis and history lookup fit the stated purpose, but the shared implementation also performs silent backend login/registration and local user-token management, which is broader than simple pet feeding analysis.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The manifest discloses automatic identity handling, but it instructs the agent not to ask or show identity values and does not clearly disclose remote account creation, credential headers, or token persistence to the installing user.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No startup persistence or destructive installer behavior was found. A development config contains a private raw-IP endpoint, but the default config points to public lifeemergence.com endpoints.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Local media upload and URL submission are expected, but the skill also reads workspace identity material, detects workspace layout, creates shared data directories, and sends identity-bearing fields to the service.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The code creates a shared SQLite user database and can store token/open_token values with no visible expiry, encryption, deletion flow, or user consent boundary.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending pet feeding media or video URLs to the configured cloud service and allowing the skill to create/reuse a backend identity, store local authentication tokens in a workspace SQLite database, and query cloud history automatically. Treat it as Review rather than malicious: I found no destructive behavior or clear exfiltration outside its configured service, but the identity and credential handling needs careful consent and scoping.
llm.findings:
[AST7] unexpected: Dynamic DAO filtering exists, but I did not find it exposed through the user-facing pet-analysis workflow; this is a code-quality risk, not the basis for the verdict.
[LP3] expected: File reads, output writes, shell execution of the packaged script, and network calls are expected for this skill, but permission and consent boundaries are not explicit enough for the identity and token handling.
[SDI-4] expected: A suppressed --open-id parameter matches the documented internal identity flow, but it increases cross-account risk if a host passes untrusted values.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Persistent identity provisioning, reading data/smyx-api-key.txt, and creating default users are implemented and only partially disclosed.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The token-bearing user database and automatic remote phoneLogin/register path are broader than the advertised analysis function and are the main Review concern.
[SQP-2] expected: Uploading local media or submitting public URLs to cloud APIs is expected and disclosed; silent account/token operations are not disclosed with comparable clarity.
[E1] unexpected: Identity-bearing data is posted to the configured backend during automatic registration/login; this is not enough for malicious intent, but it is material under-disclosure.
[P2] unexpected: A zero-width character and incomplete report-link instruction appear in SKILL.md, but I did not find hidden operational instructions or artifact-backed malicious behavior from it.
[YR4] expected: The metadata contains visible mixed-language operational instructions; this is not independently sufficient for a poisoning finding, but it compounds the need for user review.
[staticScan:suspicious.install_untrusted_source] unexpected: The raw-IP endpoint appears in config-dev.yaml and is not the default production endpoint, so I downgraded it as a standalone signal.
